research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register machine text of Executive Order 12592 (52 FR 13417, PDF pages 211-212 of the 1987-04-22 issue; sha256 137dbdd5...), whose heading line reads Executive Order 12592 of April 10, 1987 (the OCR misreads the day as 'ID'), signed April 10, 1987, titled President's Commission on Compensation of Career Federal Executives, matching the census register row (1987-04-10). Text and inventory: sections 1 through 4 are inventoried as 14 clauses (sections 1, 2 with six items, 2(b), 3, 3(b), 3(c), 4, 4(b)); the section 2(a), 3(a) and 4(a) texts sit inside the clauses headed by their section numbers, so I confirm the inventory as complete. All clauses belong to one advisory commission and end together. Ending: Executive Order 12692 section 3(b) revokes Executive Order 12592, effective September 30, 1989 (section 5). The report deadline of section 2(b) (as amended by Executive Order 12609) and the report-relative termination of section 4(b) are not ends: no held source dates the report, and the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines treats such wording as functionally spent, with express revocation as the end. Original grade: Federal Register machine text.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12692 contains no wording that preserves the order establishing the President's Commission on Compensation of Career Federal Executives: its section 1 continues other committees, its section 2 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for those other committees, and its section 3 revokes this order without exception. Reports or other work already done are completed acts; nothing continues the Commission.
